k: A card table. The felt is worn through in exactly one place: where the dealer's left hand rests.
src: 'A card table. The felt is worn through in exactly one place: where the dealer\'s left hand rests.'

k: Debits on the left, credits on the right. Debtors on the carpet.
src: 'Debits on the left, credits on the right. Debtors on the carpet.'

k: Madam Quill has never once been wrong about a number. She's been wrong about people. Twice. She keeps a ledger of that too.
src: 'Madam Quill has never once been wrong about a number. She\'s been wrong about people. Twice. She keeps a ledger of that too.'

k: Ledgers to the ceiling, each spine labeled with a year. The newest are labeled only: AFTER.
src: 'Ledgers to the ceiling, each spine labeled with a year. The newest are labeled only: AFTER.'

k: A ledger lies open to a page near the back. There is a tidy gap where one page was torn out.
src: 'A ledger lies open to a page near the back. There is a tidy gap where one page was torn out.'

k: A ledger lies open to a page near the back, worn soft with handling. ASHE, C. The column of figures runs to the bottom and over the page.
src: 'A ledger lies open to a page near the back, worn soft with handling. ASHE, C. The column of figures runs to the bottom and over the page.'

k: A small statue of a woman holding scales. Someone has balanced a coin on each pan. They are perfectly level.
src: 'A small statue of a woman holding scales. Someone has balanced a coin on each pan. They are perfectly level.'

k: LANTERNFALL — Westmost Light of Solmere.nThe Kindling: tomorrow at noon, at the Lantern.
src: 'LANTERNFALL — Westmost Light of Solmere.\nThe Kindling: tomorrow at noon, at the Lantern.'

k: They say the Hierophant hasn't left Aurenne in eleven years. And he's coming _here_. For _our_ children.
src: 'They say the Hierophant hasn\'t left Aurenne in eleven years. And he\'s coming _here_. For _our_ children.'

k: I've swept my step four times.
src: 'I\'ve swept my step four times.'

k: You got VANGUARD? That's the best one! Can I hold your sword? Can I? Just the handle?
src: 'You got VANGUARD? That\'s the best one! Can I hold your sword? Can I? Just the handle?'

k: Are you getting your Crest tomorrow? I hope I get Vanguard when I'm sixteen. Or Arcanist. Something with explosions.
src: 'Are you getting your Crest tomorrow? I hope I get Vanguard when I\'m sixteen. Or Arcanist. Something with explosions.'

k: One Crest, one life, girl. My father was a Warden, I'm a Warden, my boy's a Warden.
src: 'One Crest, one life, girl. My father was a Warden, I\'m a Warden, my boy\'s a Warden.'

k: The light knows what you are. No sense arguing with the light.
src: 'The light knows what you are. No sense arguing with the light.'

k: My Tamsy got Mender last spring. Cried for a week — she wanted Cantor.
src: 'My Tamsy got Mender last spring. Cried for a week — she wanted Cantor.'

k: She's good at it now, though. Funny how the light knows.
src: 'She\'s good at it now, though. Funny how the light knows.'

k: That white ship's got sails like an angel's wings. Never seen the like.
src: 'That white ship\'s got sails like an angel\'s wings. Never seen the like.'

k: Nor such a quiet crew.
src: 'Nor such a quiet crew.'

k: Tide's out further than I've ever seen. You can walk to the eel rocks.
src: 'Tide\'s out further than I\'ve ever seen. You can walk to the eel rocks.'

k: The sea's waiting for something.
src: 'The sea\'s waiting for something.'

k: Any minute now! The Hierophant's ship! I've been here since dawn.
src: 'Any minute now! The Hierophant\'s ship! I\'ve been here since dawn.'

k: If you see white sails, scream. I will too. We'll scream together.
src: 'If you see white sails, scream. I will too. We\'ll scream together.'

k: Tobias says the net's with Brisa. Tobias says a lot of things.
src: 'Tobias says the net\'s with Brisa. Tobias says a lot of things.'

k: Good luck tomorrow, love. Whatever the light says, you're still our Wren.
src: 'Good luck tomorrow, love. Whatever the light says, you\'re still our Wren.'

k: The village well. Someone has carved WREN + ILSE + THE SEA into the stone. You remember carving it.
src: 'The village well. Someone has carved WREN + ILSE + THE SEA into the stone. You remember carving it.'

k: Your mother's herb garden. Rosemary, thyme, and a sea-lavender that has never once flowered.
src: 'Your mother\'s herb garden. Rosemary, thyme, and a sea-lavender that has never once flowered.'

k: No time for the caves now.
src: 'No time for the caves now.'

k: Not in this storm.
src: 'Not in this storm.'

k: The tide caves... Mom would kill me. I should do my chores first.
src: 'The tide caves... Mom would kill me. I should do my chores first.'

k: Your father's books. Sea charts, star charts, a novel about a pirate queen with the last chapter torn out.
src: 'Your father\'s books. Sea charts, star charts, a novel about a pirate queen with the last chapter torn out.'

k: A shelf of your own books. Every one has washed ashore at some point. Most of them are still a little salty.
src: 'A shelf of your own books. Every one has washed ashore at some point. Most of them are still a little salty.'

k: Two plates. There have been two plates for seven years.
src: 'Two plates. There have been two plates for seven years.'

k: Nana's been up since four, stewing kelp for tomorrow. The whole house smells like a tide pool.
src: 'Nana\'s been up since four, stewing kelp for tomorrow. The whole house smells like a tide pool.'

k: Jars of dried herbs, labeled in Ilse's tiny, exact handwriting. One just says: DO NOT. LET WREN. TOUCH.
src: 'Jars of dried herbs, labeled in Ilse\'s tiny, exact handwriting. One just says: DO NOT. LET WREN. TOUCH.'

k: A cauldron of something green. It smells, generously, like the sea.
src: 'A cauldron of something green. It smells, generously, like the sea.'

k: A bed and a bowl of chowder, love? Ten gold.
src: 'A bed and a bowl of chowder, love? Ten gold.'

k: —and THEN I said, "Not today, Gloam-beast!" and I— oh! Wren. Ilse. Hello.
src: '—and THEN I said, "Not today, Gloam-beast!" and I— oh! Wren. Ilse. Hello.'

k: I was just telling these children about my many heroic deeds. All true. Mostly true. True in spirit.
src: 'I was just telling these children about my many heroic deeds. All true. Mostly true. True in spirit.'

k: Big day tomorrow! Don't worry about the Kindling. The light's never wrong. Mine said Warden and look at me. ...Don't look too closely.
src: 'Big day tomorrow! Don\'t worry about the Kindling. The light\'s never wrong. Mine said Warden and look at me. ...Don\'t look too closely.'

k: Bram says he fought a Gloam-beast with a spoon!
src: 'Bram says he fought a Gloam-beast with a spoon!'

k: Came in from Port Gale last week. Mainland's jumpy. Talk of shadows in the Whisperwold. Lights going out in villages.
src: 'Came in from Port Gale last week. Mainland\'s jumpy. Talk of shadows in the Whisperwold. Lights going out in villages.'

k: Folk say the Lanterns are getting tired. Like old men.
src: 'Folk say the Lanterns are getting tired. Like old men.'

k: Tonics, charms, a sword or two. Kindling special: everything's the same price as always.
src: 'Tonics, charms, a sword or two. Kindling special: everything\'s the same price as always.'

k: A crate of salted fish and a note: "MAELA — DON'T." Below it, in different handwriting: "I DID."
src: 'A crate of salted fish and a note: "MAELA — DON\'T." Below it, in different handwriting: "I DID."'
